candidates.summary: Artificial Analysis launched v2.0 of its Coding Agent Index, which scores models together with their agent harnesses; Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 61.7.
facts: The index covers 290 tasks across three equally weighted benchmarks.
FrontierCode v1.1 from Cognition replaces DeepSWE.
Runner-ups: Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) 59.3, Muse Code with Muse Wonder Full 58.9, Claude Code with Claude Fable 5.1 57.6.
On FrontierCode, Opus 5.5 scores 56.0%, ahead of Codex with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 52.6%.
SWE-Atlas-QnA grading was revised: 127 of 1,306 rubric criteria reworded, with GPT-6 Luna (xhigh) as judge.

candidates.summary: A critical advisory (CVE-2026-96620, CVSS 9.2) in the Claude Agent SDK for Python: a resume value starting with '-' could inject --mcp-config and lead to arbitrary command execution. Fixed in claude-agent-sdk 0.2.121.
facts: Affected: claude-agent-sdk (pip) versions below 0.2.121.
Fixed in 0.2.121 via PR #1123; the TypeScript SDK fix shipped in 0.3.208.

candidates.summary: Mistral released Voxtral 3 speech models plus a voice agent SDK built on LiveKit for Python and TypeScript.
facts: Speech-to-text covers 50+ languages with diarization and end-of-turn detection.
Text-to-speech covers 35+ languages; Pro Voice builds a custom voice from 30 minutes of audio.
Available through Mistral's EU API or self-deployment.

candidates.summary: Google introduced the Gemini API CLI (gemini-api), a stateless binary that lets Codex, Claude Code or any agent with shell access call Gemini models, media generation, file analysis and background managed agents.
facts: Self-describing interface: request schemas via --schema and machine-readable usage via --usage are built into the binary.
--dry-run validates inputs and prints the resolved HTTP request with credentials redacted, without a network call.
Apache 2.0 licensed.

candidates.summary: Google Cloud announced Agent Compute Engine, the microVM service that already powers Gemini agents, giving each agent a hardware-isolated sandbox; preview is targeted for the coming months.
facts: Announced at AGNTCon + MCPCon on Oct 22; it already powers Gemini as an agent for work tasks.
Idle microVMs are paused via checkpoint and restore while the agent waits on a human or external system; copy-on-write memory sharing runs multiple agents on one OS template.
Each microVM runs with its agent's own identity and short-lived credentials; service credentials are injected at egress outside the microVM; runs on Google's Titanium IPU.
Each microVM gets its own Hyperdisk for persistent workspaces and agent context.

candidates.summary: Matt Pocock highlights content mappers in the TypeScript 7.1 Beta: import non-TypeScript files (markdown, vue, svelte), extract types with a mapper, run tsc with --runExternalCode, and get type inference from them.
facts: Simplest case per the post: import a markdown file, add config to tsconfig.json, run tsc with --runExternalCode, get fully typed frontmatter.
TypeScript 7.1 Beta was announced Oct 20 with a preview API and content mapper support.

candidates.summary: Perplexity's 4B decision model (pplx-decider-flash-v1.2) now runs locally on a Mac through a Decider for Mac app, with no API key and no data leaving the machine.
facts: Ask a question about text or an image and get a probability back, on device (perplexitydevs).
Aravind Srinivas framed it as an example of open-weight, compact models.

candidates.summary: DoorDash paper: a multi-agent LLM system that cleans up stale feature flags end to end (live rollout data via MCP, Jira tickets, PR creation) produced engineer-approved PRs for 45 of 50 stale flags.
facts: DoorDash has 56,000+ feature flags across 623 repositories; 1,659 were stale as of May 2026.
Average cost per cleanup was $4.79 and 13.8 minutes, versus internal estimates of 1-2 hours per manual cleanup.
Rule-based cleanup tools proved insufficient in DoorDash's codebases.

candidates.summary: AgentPhishing benchmark: LLM email agents handle known phishing emails safely but fail against attacks optimized for agent behavior; four of nine agents tested detected under 10% and complied with malicious requests over 45% of the time.
facts: Authors built PhishOpt, which optimizes reusable email-generation skills against individual agents under realism constraints.
Failures were analyzed using Cialdini's persuasion principles.

candidates.summary: Paper: a naive RAG baseline over raw conversation history (dense retrieval plus reranking) ranked first among compared memory systems in six of seven benchmark-model settings, beating the strongest agentic memory system by 0.13-5.53 points.
facts: Benchmarks: LoCoMo, LongMemEval, MEME and MemoryAgentBench.
Even full access to transformed memory stores left an accuracy gap versus raw evidence.

candidates.summary: Replit says it patched infrastructure, updated language tooling and blocked exploits to protect hosted apps from recent third-party vulnerabilities, applying fixes automatically where possible and notifying users who need to republish.

kloss_xyz posted a step-by-step setup for running Claude Code from an iPhone: Claude Max subscription, Claude Mac app signed in to Claude Code with a repo on a plugged-in laptop, then the Claude iPhone app's Claude Code tab.
Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus, reviewed by the WSJ and Reuters, shows $16.3B in first-half 2026 revenue and an $80.7B net loss, about $72B of it a non-cash charge tied to convertible notes.
facts: First-half net loss a year earlier was $13B.
Compute spend was nearly $9B in the first half, up from $2.3B.
Anthropic has at least $518B in commitments over a decade, per Reuters; WSJ reports it could spend $750B on compute.

candidates.summary: eMudhra's board decided to withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business after a recent incident with its CAs, which it says it revoked within 14 hours of discovery.
facts: eMudhra says no end-entity certificates were issued from the affected CAs and its infrastructure was not compromised.
Global SSL/TLS is about 1% of eMudhra's revenue, per the release.
Go added a crypto/x509 denylist for the intermediates no longer considered trustworthy (CVE-2026-111943).
The HN thread on the exit reached 1,077 points.

candidates.summary: Guillermo Rauch: this week a key held by stewards of the internet's encryption had a password of just "4"; he says it could be used to target and decrypt nearly everything and residual risk is still being cleaned up.
The Atlantic profiles Ondřej Surý, a relatively anonymous volunteer working on PHP security, under the headline 'If Anything Happens to This Guy … Everyone Is Screwed'.
Meta launched its Muse assistant in Japan, and a $100,000 Open Kernel Challenge invites developers to make Muse Spark run fastest.
facts: Alexandr Wang: Muse is available in Japan now from app stores.
Wang also said 1Password is coming to Muse, rolling out over the coming days.
The Verge reports Meta re-enabled Muse sharing after researchers found public conversation links were easy to find.

related.name: The Verge: Meta turns Muse sharing back on

candidates.summary: Elon Musk: Grok Bot now integrates with your phone apps.

related.name: poteto: use Grok Bot with native phone apps

candidates.summary: Arc Institute preprint uses genome language models and AI agents to find new candidate functional RNAs in the genome's non-coding regions.
facts: Patrick Collison: it uses deep learning and model interpretability to productive ends on a totally different kind of knowledge.
Patrick Hsu: RNAs can keep similar structures and functions while their DNA sequences change dramatically, which conventional computational tools struggle to recognize.

candidates.summary: Paper: an Agent Delegability Index across 146 countries finds 35.2% of task time in world employment is at least partly delegable to AI agents in 2026, and only 2.5% fully.
facts: Delegable employment rises with income: 22.5% in low-income countries vs 48.7% in high-income countries.
Full delegation peaks for tasks that take a human about 11.8 minutes.
Across 101 countries, delegability and observed AI usage correlate at r = 0.86.
The index, prompts and an MCP server are released on GitHub.

candidates.summary: Gary Marcus (contrarian) writes that CoreWeave stock has dropped over 50% in the last six months.
Tavi Costa: the dollar's muted response during the selloff was arguably the most important thing today; treasuries aside, the dollar would normally have caught a strong bid.
Nathan Benaich shares a RAAIS talk by Alasdair Russell (University of Cambridge) on why AI can accelerate research yet leave the last 20% as the bottleneck.
Headline via Google News: Bitcoin treasury firm Metaplanet names Capital Research its largest major shareholder.

Meng To built landing pages (three keyboard sites, a SaaS page, a rainy 3D Singapore at night and a 3D lighthouse game) with MiniMax M3.1 Flash, priced at $0.15 per 1M input and $0.60 per 1M output tokens, and shared the whole process with prompts.
The Verge: Canva launched Canva Craft, its first in-house image model, which uses a two-stage architecture to plan a design before generating it.
